speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether there are existing regulations on the practice of "overboarding" in Singapore, where individuals hold more board directorships than they can responsibly handle; and (b) if there are none, whether the Government will study introducing such regulations for Singapore-incorporated or Singapore-listed companies.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And I thank the Senior Minister of State for his reply.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Before that, I declare my interest as a board director of a Singapore company.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Would the Government consider adopting a more prescriptive approach given the fact that there is research that demonstrates that the more board directorships one holds, the less time one can devote to discharging one's responsibilities as a director effectively and also given international precedence?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In the United Kingdom (UK), I believe, they do adopt a more prescriptive approach.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The UK Corporate Governance Code 2018 which is a promulgated by the Financial Reporting Council, sets certain concrete limits.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For example, you are full-time executive director, you cannot hold more than one non-executive directorship of the Financial Times Stock Exchange (FTSE) 100 company.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In the United States (US), while there are no regulations, asset managers and institutional investors also do have a threshold number for the maximum number of directorships that a board director should have before it is considered "overboarding".

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The point that Mr Perera made about the US – and for that matter Australia and Hong Kong – they also do not set a limit under the law for the number of directorships that a person can hold.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But that the responsibility for the individuals, the directors, to be able to discharge their responsibilities diligently, I think that is common across all these jurisdictions.
